requirements.title: IEEE_SCALB overflow signals and returns the specified signed extreme
requirements.definition: For finite X with X*2**I too large, IEEE_OVERFLOW occurs; the result is signed infinity with IEEE infinity support and otherwise SIGN(HUGE(X),X).

pending.IEEE_SCALB-overflow-signals: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(HUGE(1.0)), IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_OVERFLOW,1.0), and FLAG-HALTING-OFF(IEEE_OVERFLOW,1.0) before the call; supported branch clears all supported flags, evaluates IEEE_SCALB(HUGE(1.0),1), and asserts IEEE_OVERFLOW signaling. Mutation uses I=0.
pending.IEEE_SCALB-overflow-infinity-result: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(HUGE(1.0)), IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(-HUGE(1.0)), IEEE_SUPPORT_INF(1.0), and IEEE_CLASS observer support before the calls; supported branch evaluates IEEE_SCALB(HUGE(1.0),1) and IEEE_SCALB(-HUGE(1.0),1) and asserts positive and negative infinity classes. Mutation expects finite HUGE.
pending.IEEE_SCALB-overflow-huge-result-without-: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(HUGE(1.0)), IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(-HUGE(1.0)), and a false IEEE_SUPPORT_INF(1.0) result before the calls; supported branch evaluates IEEE_SCALB(HUGE(1.0),1) and IEEE_SCALB(-HUGE(1.0),1) and asserts SIGN(HUGE(X),X) for positive and negative X. Infinity-supported branch skips this facet. Mutation expects infinity.

requirements.title: IEEE_SCALB underflow signals and returns nearest signed representable result
requirements.definition: For X*2**I too small with loss of accuracy, IEEE_UNDERFLOW occurs and the result is the nearest representable magnitude with the sign of X.

pending.IEEE_SCALB-underflow-signals: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(TINY(1.0)), IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,1.0), FLAG-HALTING-OFF(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,1.0), RADIX(1.0)==2, and subnormal support before the call; supported branch clears all supported flags, evaluates IEEE_SCALB(TINY(1.0),-DIGITS(1.0)-1), and asserts IEEE_UNDERFLOW signaling. Mutation uses I=0.
pending.IEEE_SCALB-underflow-nearest-signed-resu: Guarded branch probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(-TINY(1.0)), IEEE_IS_NEGATIVE observer support, RADIX(1.0)==2, and subnormal support before the call; supported branch hand-checks TINY(1.0)*2**(-DIGITS(1.0)-1) as one quarter of the smallest subnormal, evaluates IEEE_SCALB(-TINY(1.0),-DIGITS(1.0)-1), and asserts equality to zero plus IEEE_IS_NEGATIVE true. Mutation uses positive X.

Argument restrictions split X type and I type.

Example is illustrative; the exact scaling case is already planned from p6.
